# Platform & Console knowledge brief

Platform & Console owns inference gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and the operator-facing console. # Platform & Console knowledge brief

Platform & Console owns inference gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and the operator-facing console. The team uses LiteLLM for gateway work and Langfuse for observability and console workflows, reconciling code changes with product, security, and operational requirements.

## High-value source areas

These are retrieval hints, not access-control filters.

- codebases/litellm
- codebases/langfuse
- github/rbac-policy-bundle
- linear/engineering
- linear/design
- confluence/eng-platform
- confluence/product-docs
- slack/eng-platform
- slack/product

Lead: Priya Natarajan

## Representative sources in this corpus

- `dsid_3bf458c6f7e941d1b2b7929e4e796af4` — Introduce scoped service profiles, KMS claim mirroring, and audit hinting (`sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-100101-introduce-scoped-service-profiles-kms-claim-mirroring-and-audit-hinting.json`)

    "id": "dsid_f954519b2b004d20acf952719135340a",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/embedded-onboarding-playbook-for-product-and-platform-teams-2026.json",
    "title": "Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams\",\n  \"space\": \"company-handbook\",\n  \"author\": \"Anika Rao\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"people-ops\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-06-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2027-02-14\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Daniel Kim\",\n    \"Priya Mehta\",\n    \"Javier Morales\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"onboarding\",\n    \"embedded\",\n    \"manager-guide\",\n    \"tools\",\n    \"roles\",\n    \"checklist\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-access-and-career-checkpoints-2025\",\n    \"company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"Overview:\\\\n\\\\nPurpose\\\\nThis playbook defines a repeatable, lightweight embedded onboarding pattern tailored for hires joining Product and Platform teams at Redwood. It aligns role ramp expectations, tooling access timelines, manager and mentor responsibilities, and a standardized handover template so new joiners reach measurable impact faster while minimizing operational friction.\\\\n\\\\nScope\\\\n- Applies to full-time ICs (levels IC1\\u2013IC5) and engineering managers joining Product, Platform, and Core infra teams.\\\\n- Not a replacement for team-specific PRDs or technical deep dives; it supplements those with operational and people processes.\\\\n\\\\nOwners and Escalation\\\\n- Playbook owner: People Ops (Anika Rao).\\\\n- Tier 1 operational owner for tooling: Platform Operations (SRE) team.\\\\n- Escalation: raise to People Ops if provisioning SLAs exceed thresholds (see Access SLA section).\\\\n\\\\nPrinciples\\\\n1) Predictable first 30 days: reduce variability across teams with a 0\\u201330 day milestone map.\\\\n2) Role-tailored but consistent: core checkpoints are uniform; technical ramp content varies by team.\\\\n3) Manager-driven outcomes, mentor-supported development: managers set goals; mentors help reduce cognitive overhead.\\\\n4) Automated, auditable provisioning: avoid ad-hoc access requests.\\\\n\\\\nQuick Start (for hiring manager)\\\\n1. Fill the Embedded Onboarding Form (People Ops template) at offer acceptance.\\\\n2. Assign a primary mentor and a technical buddy before Day 0.\\\\n3. Confirm required tool access and sensitive systems with Platform Ops within 48 hours.\\\\n4. Publish the 90-day success criteria in the team\\u2019s workspace.\\\\n\\\\nPreboarding Checklist (to complete before Day 0)\\\\n- Offer paperwork processed and payroll setup confirmed.\\\\n- Laptop chosen and procurement ticket created (include required GPU/VM specs if applicable).\\\\n- Identity (SSO) account created with base groups: contributor, slack, okta.\\\\n- Read-ahead packet sent (team charter, current roadmap, recent design reviews).\\\\n- First-week calendar blocks created: 1:1s, team orientation, mentor syncs.\\\\n\\\\nDay 0\\u20131: Immediate Priorities\\\\n- 1:1 with manager (goal-setting and success criteria).\\\\n- Intro to mentor and buddy: schedule recurring check-ins (2x/week first month).\\\\n- Verify basic access (email, Slack, docs, code repo read).\\\\n- Run start script: redwood-setup onboard --confirm (see Examples).\\\\n\\\\nWeek 1\\u20132: Build Context and Triage Access\\\\n- Complete team architecture walkthrough and architecture docs.\\\\n- Shadow a deployment/release and an on-call rotation (platform hires).\\\\n- Confirm additional service-specific access (service accounts, deploy keys).\\\\n- Deliverable: short note in team channel summarizing understanding and questions.\\\\n\\\\nWeeks 3\\u20138: First Scoped Deliverable\\\\n- Owner and manager agree a scoped ticket that can land in 2\\u20134 weeks.\\\\n- Weekly progress updates in the team\\u2019s sprint channel.\\\\n- Mentor assists with PR/CR reviews to speed feedback loop.\\\\n\\\\n90-Day Outcomes (expected)\\\\n- New hire has delivered at least one scoped change and conducted a knowledge share.\\\\n- Manager has documented performance and learning plan for next 90 days.\\\\n- People Ops closes onboarding loop and records completion.\\\\n\\\\nRole-Specific Orientation (high level)\\\\n- Product Engineers: focus first week on product metrics, user flows, A/B test signals, and feature flags.\\\\n- Platform Engineers: focus first week on CI/CD pipelines, infra dashboards, incident runbooks, and capacity controls.\\\\n- Product Managers joining engineering teams: ramp on metrics, release cadence, and Git workflow for PRs and specs.\\\\n\\\\nManager Responsibilities (checklist)\\\\n- Provide 90-day success criteria in writing by Day 1.\\\\n- Allocate a mentor and schedule recurring check-ins.\\\\n- Create a scoped deliverable and acceptance criteria by the end of Week 2.\\\\n- Ensure access requests are filed within first 48 hours and follow up to meet SLAs.\\\\n\\\\nMentor/Buddy Responsibilities\\\\n- First two weeks: daily ad-hoc availability and twice-weekly structured syncs.\\\\n- Review first three PRs within 48 hours.\\\\n- Facilitate introductions to core collaborators.\\\\n\\\\nTools & Access Matrix (example)\\\\n| System | Base Access (Day 0\\u20131) | Role-Specific Access | Owner | SLA |\\\\n|--------|-----------------------|----------------------|-------|-----|\\\\n| Slack | Member | N/A | People Ops | 0\\u20131 day |\\\\n| Confluence/docs | Read | Write (after training) | People Ops | 0\\u20131 day |\\\\n| Git (repos) | Read on team repos | Write on assigned repos | Eng DevEx | 0\\u20132 days |\\\\n| CI/CD (deploy) | No | Approve/Deploy for platform | Platform Ops | 2\\u20137 days |\\\\n| Cloud console (prod) | No | IAM role-based access | Cloud Infra | 2\\u201310 days |\\\\n| Monitoring/Dashboards | View | Alerting edit after training | SRE | 1\\u20135 days |\\\\n\\\\nAccess SLA and Request Process\\\\n- Standard SLA targets:\\\\n  - Base access (email, Slack, docs): 24 hours.\\\\n  - Repository write and monitoring view: 48\\u201372 hours.\\\\n  - Production console or service accounts: up to 10 business days (require approval).\\\\n- To request access: file ticket in Platform Ops queue with template: subject \\\\\\\"Access request: <name> \\u2014 <system>\\\\\\\" and include manager approval.\\\\n- Escalation path: after SLA misses of 48 hours for base access, People Ops will intervene.\\\\n\\\\nHandover and Knowledge Transfer Standards\\\\n- All handovers must include: short context paragraph, why change matters, architectural pointers, test coverage notes, and rollback steps.\\\\n- Use the team\\u2019s Handover Template (copyable from People Ops) and include at least one short demo recording (5\\u201310 minutes).\\\\n\\\\nHandover Template (pasteable)\\\\n1. Title and owner\\\\n2. Brief description and business impact\\\\n3. Key services and repos\\\\n4. Runbook excerpt and common failure modes\\\\n5. How to validate a successful change\\\\n6. Contacts and escalation path\\\\n\\\\nExamples and CLI snippets\\\\n- Example: quick local setup (developer machine):\\\\n  1) git clone git@github.com:redwood/<team-repo>.git\\\\n  2) ./scripts/setup-dev.sh --minimal\\\\n  3) export REDWOOD_ENV=dev && ./bin/start-local\\\\n- Example: access bootstrap (internal CLI):\\\\n  $ redwood-iam request --user anika@redwood.com --role repo-write --reason \\\\\\\"onboarding product team\\\\\\\"\\\\n  # check status\\\\n  $ redwood-iam status --request-id RQ-12345\\\\n\\\\nMeasurement and Feedback\\\\n- People Ops will run a 30-day survey to measure ramp clarity, tool access friction, and mentor effectiveness.\\\\n- Key metrics: time-to-first-merge, time-to-deploy, Days-to-base-access (median).\\\\n- Quarterly retro: managers and mentors meet to refine the embedded onboarding checklist.\\\\n\\\\nCommon Pitfalls and Mitigations\\\\n- Pitfall: missing service accounts delaying development. Mitigation: copy standard service-account request during preboarding.\\\\n- Pitfall: overloaded mentors. Mitigation: cap active mentees to 2 per mentor and use rotation windows.\\\\n\\\\nAppendix A \\u2014 Template: 90-Day Success Criteria (example)\\\\n- Objective: Complete a cross-team bug fix that traverses frontend, backend, and infra validation and ship with documentation.\\\\n- Success metrics: PR merged, automated tests green, deployment to staging, and a short knowledge share recorded.\\\\n\\\\nAppendix B \\u2014 Suggested Onboarding Reading List\\\\n- Team README and architecture map\\\\n- Last three release notes and postmortems\\\\n- API contracts and SLOs for services you will own\\\\n\\\\nFrequently Asked Questions\\\\nQ: Who signs off when accesses are delayed?\\\\nA: The hiring manager and People Ops. For production-level access, Cloud Infra approval is required.\\\\n\\\\nQ: Can a mentor be from a different team?\\\\nA: Yes \\u2014 cross-team mentors are encouraged if they reduce context-switching and are familiar with the core tech stack.\\\\n\\\\nRelated resources\\\\n- People Ops: onboarding form and templates\\\\n- Platform Ops: access request flow and SLAs\\\\n- Team workspace: add the new hire to the team\\u2019s onboarding page\\\\n\\\\nLast review notes\\\\n- 2027-02-14: Updated access SLA targets and added example CLI commands. (Anika Rao)\\\\n\\\\nContact\\\\nPeople Ops (onboarding): onboarding@redwood.com\\\\nPlatform Ops (access requests): platform-ops@redwood.com\\\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_f954519b2b004d20acf952719135340a\"\n}",

document.title: Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams
document.content:
{
  "title": "Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams",
  "space": "company-handbook",
  "author": "Anika Rao",
  "owner_team": "people-ops",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-06-15",
  "last_updated": "2027-02-14",
  "reviewers": [
    "Daniel Kim",
    "Priya Mehta",
    "Javier Morales"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "onboarding",
    "embedded",
    "manager-guide",
    "tools",
    "roles",
    "checklist"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-access-and-career-checkpoints-2025",
    "company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "Overview:\\n\\nPurpose\\nThis playbook defines a repeatable, lightweight embedded onboarding pattern tailored for hires joining Product and Platform teams at Redwood. It aligns role ramp expectations, tooling access timelines, manager and mentor responsibilities, and a standardized handover template so new joiners reach measurable impact faster while minimizing operational friction.\\n\\nScope\\n- Applies to full-time ICs (levels IC1\u2013IC5) and engineering managers joining Product, Platform, and Core infra teams.\\n- Not a replacement for team-specific PRDs or technical deep dives; it supplements those with operational and people processes.\\n\\nOwners and Escalation\\n- Playbook owner: People Ops (Anika Rao).\\n- Tier 1 operational owner for tooling: Platform Operations (SRE) team.\\n- Escalation: raise to People Ops if provisioning SLAs exceed thresholds (see Access SLA section).\\n\\nPrinciples\\n1) Predictable first 30 days: reduce variability across teams with a 0\u201330 day milestone map.\\n2) Role-tailored but consistent: core checkpoints are uniform; technical ramp content varies by team.\\n3) Manager-driven outcomes, mentor-supported development: managers set goals; mentors help reduce cognitive overhead.\\n4) Automated, auditable provisioning: avoid ad-hoc access requests.\\n\\nQuick Start (for hiring manager)\\n1. Fill the Embedded Onboarding Form (People Ops template) at offer acceptance.\\n2. Assign a primary mentor and a technical buddy before Day 0.\\n3. Confirm required tool access and sensitive systems with Platform Ops within 48 hours.\\n4. Publish the 90-day success criteria in the team\u2019s workspace.\\n\\nPreboarding Checklist (to complete before Day 0)\\n- Offer paperwork processed and payroll setup confirmed.\\n- Laptop chosen and procurement ticket created (include required GPU/VM specs if applicable).\\n- Identity (SSO) account created with base groups: contributor, slack, okta.\\n- Read-ahead packet sent (team charter, current roadmap, recent design reviews).\\n- First-week calendar blocks created: 1:1s, team orientation, mentor syncs.\\n\\nDay 0\u20131: Immediate Priorities\\n- 1:1 with manager (goal-setting and success criteria).\\n- Intro to mentor and buddy: schedule recurring check-ins (2x/week first month).\\n- Verify basic access (email, Slack, docs, code repo read).\\n- Run start script: redwood-setup onboard --confirm (see Examples).\\n\\nWeek 1\u20132: Build Context and Triage Access\\n- Complete team architecture walkthrough and architecture docs.\\n- Shadow a deployment/release and an on-call rotation (platform hires).\\n- Confirm additional service-specific access (service accounts, deploy keys).\\n- Deliverable: short note in team channel summarizing understanding and questions.\\n\\nWeeks 3\u20138: First Scoped Deliverable\\n- Owner and manager agree a scoped ticket that can land in 2\u20134 weeks.\\n- Weekly progress updates in the team\u2019s sprint channel.\\n- Mentor assists with PR/CR reviews to speed feedback loop.\\n\\n90-Day Outcomes (expected)\\n- New hire has delivered at least one scoped change and conducted a knowledge share.\\n- Manager has documented performance and learning plan for next 90 days.\\n- People Ops closes onboarding loop and records completion.\\n\\nRole-Specific Orientation (high level)\\n- Product Engineers: focus first week on product metrics, user flows, A/B test signals, and feature flags.\\n- Platform Engineers: focus first week on CI/CD pipelines, infra dashboards, incident runbooks, and capacity controls.\\n- Product Managers joining engineering teams: ramp on metrics, release cadence, and Git workflow for PRs and specs.\\n\\nManager Responsibilities (checklist)\\n- Provide 90-day success criteria in writing by Day 1.\\n- Allocate a mentor and schedule recurring check-ins.\\n- Create a scoped deliverable and acceptance criteria by the end of Week 2.\\n- Ensure access requests are filed within first 48 hours and follow up to meet SLAs.\\n\\nMentor/Buddy Responsibilities\\n- First two weeks: daily ad-hoc availability and twice-weekly structured syncs.\\n- Review first three PRs within 48 hours.\\n- Facilitate introductions to core collaborators.\\n\\nTools & Access Matrix (example)\\n| System | Base Access (Day 0\u20131) | Role-Specific Access | Owner | SLA |\\n|--------|-----------------------|----------------------|-------|-----|\\n| Slack | Member | N/A | People Ops | 0\u20131 day |\\n| Confluence/docs | Read | Write (after training) | People Ops | 0\u20131 day |\\n| Git (repos) | Read on team repos | Write on assigned repos | Eng DevEx | 0\u20132 days |\\n| CI/CD (deploy) | No | Approve/Deploy for platform | Platform Ops | 2\u20137 days |\\n| Cloud console (prod) | No | IAM role-based access | Cloud Infra | 2\u201310 days |\\n| Monitoring/Dashboards | View | Alerting edit after training | SRE | 1\u20135 days |\\n\\nAccess SLA and Request Process\\n- Standard SLA targets:\\n  - Base access (email, Slack, docs): 24 hours.\\n  - Repository write and monitoring view: 48\u201372 hours.\\n  - Production console or service accounts: up to 10 business days (require approval).\\n- To request access: file ticket in Platform Ops queue with template: subject \\\"Access request: <name> \u2014 <system>\\\" and include manager approval.\\n- Escalation path: after SLA misses of 48 hours for base access, People Ops will intervene.\\n\\nHandover and Knowledge Transfer Standards\\n- All handovers must include: short context paragraph, why change matters, architectural pointers, test coverage notes, and rollback steps.\\n- Use the team\u2019s Handover Template (copyable from People Ops) and include at least one short demo recording (5\u201310 minutes).\\n\\nHandover Template (pasteable)\\n1. Title and owner\\n2. Brief description and business impact\\n3. Key services and repos\\n4. Runbook excerpt and common failure modes\\n5. How to validate a successful change\\n6. Contacts and escalation path\\n\\nExamples and CLI snippets\\n- Example: quick local setup (developer machine):\\n  1) git clone git@github.com:redwood/<team-repo>.git\\n  2) ./scripts/setup-dev.sh --minimal\\n  3) export REDWOOD_ENV=dev && ./bin/start-local\\n- Example: access bootstrap (internal CLI):\\n  $ redwood-iam request --user anika@redwood.com --role repo-write --reason \\\"onboarding product team\\\"\\n  # check status\\n  $ redwood-iam status --request-id RQ-12345\\n\\nMeasurement and Feedback\\n- People Ops will run a 30-day survey to measure ramp clarity, tool access friction, and mentor effectiveness.\\n- Key metrics: time-to-first-merge, time-to-deploy, Days-to-base-access (median).\\n- Quarterly retro: managers and mentors meet to refine the embedded onboarding checklist.\\n\\nCommon Pitfalls and Mitigations\\n- Pitfall: missing service accounts delaying development. Mitigation: copy standard service-account request during preboarding.\\n- Pitfall: overloaded mentors. {

  "conversation": [
    "Hiro Tanaka: reproduce the behavior against the pinned source tree and attach a minimal evidence artifact.",
    "Sofia Ivanova: separate upstream behavior, Redwood compatibility policy, and incident mitigation in the decision.",
    "Ethan Park: require rollback criteria and an upstream issue or contribution link before promotion."
  ],
  "created_at": "2026-01-17",
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "infra_b0bb081732d3f8b2ab8b16f16d248328",
  "description": "Redwood Inference maintains langfuse/langfuse as an upstream-first infrastructure dependency. This record belongs to shared-upstream-governance-incident-response: Coordinate upstream issue response, incident containment, release qualification, and durable contribution policy across both dependencies. The working evidence is langfuse/langfuse#12736 https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/12736. Owen Phillips qualifies the pinned upstream behavior, uses a temporary downstream patch only when an operational boundary requires it, and records contribution, removal, and rollback criteria before rollout. Company context: # Company Overview: Redwood Inference\n\n## Company name + 1\u2011liner\n**Redwood Inference** is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.\n\n## Mission and thesis\n**Mission:** Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.\n\n**Thesis:** As LLM capabilities and open model ecosystems expand, competitive advantage shifts from model ownership to *serving*: latency, cost, reliability, deployment flexibility, and operational tooling. The winners will provide a unified runtime and developer experience that makes inference predictable and economical across rapidly changing  Initiative context: Perf baseline & representative workload suite: Establish Q1 2026 latency/throughput baselines across top models and traffic shapes.\nMixed-workload scheduler prototype: Implement and test a short/long prompt scheduling policy to reduce p95 tail latency.\nRuntime LTS branch & release process: Stand up an enterprise LTS channel with slower-change release notes and backport policy.\n# Reliability Program (SLOs, Incident Reduction, Graceful Degradation)\nTiered SLO definitions + error budget policy: Define availability/latency/error SLOs per Hosted/Dedicated tier and enforce error budgets.\nIncident taxonomy + ownership mapping: Classify top incident types and assign primary owners and remediation SLAs.\nStatus page transparency upgrades: Improve component granularity, incident comms templates, and post-incident summaries.\nIncident bot + diagnostics improvements: Enhance automated context gatherin Connector guidance: Directory:\nsources/github\n\nTarget number of files:\n8000\n\nFile name format:\nThe files should start with \"pr-\" (since they're all Pull Request) followed by a few digits and a short description of the PR (e.g. pr-18345-address-parallelism-bottleneck-in-gpu-inference.json).\n\nContent rules:\n- All of the PRs must be associated with one of the repos (directories). It cannot be at the top level directly under github.\n- This directory represents GitHub artifacts, modeled as pull requests (PRs).\n- Each document corresponds to exactly one pull request.\n- Repository distribution:\n  - Redwood Inference is  Pinned source: langfuse/langfuse@c4eaf1f4c0cd1851f0c9dbea2802c243cf787a09. Public record excerpt: issue #12736. ### Describe the bug\n\n### Describe the bug\nWhen ingesting historical traces via the REST API (`/api/public/ingestion`) using a custom JSON batch payload, the new V3 \"Faster Langfuse experience\" UI fails to render the Latency pill and Tags array on the right-hand panel. \n\nHowever, when toggling the Preview UI OFF (returning to the Stable UI), the Latency pill and Tags render perfectly. It appears the new UI requires an OpenTelemetry-specific envelope to render these components, causing a degradation for users relying on the REST API for asynchronous/historical ETL ingestion.\n\n\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n### To Reproduce\n1. Ingest a trace via `POST /api/public/ingestion`.\n2. Include `startTime`, `endTime`, and a `tags` array in the trace-create JSON body.\n3. Open the trace with the **Preview UI enabled**. Notice the Latency and Tags are missing from the right panel (though total time appears",

    "content": "{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"google_drive\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Logan Wright\",\n    \"Chloe Martin\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Working notes\\n\\nRedwood Inference maintains langfuse/langfuse as an upstream-first infrastructure dependency. This record belongs to shared-upstream-governance-incident-response: Coordinate upstream issue response, incident containment, release qualification, and durable contribution policy across both dependencies. The working evidence is langfuse/langfuse#12736 https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/12736. Renee Sullivan qualifies the pinned upstream behavior, uses a temporary downstream patch only when an operational boundary requires it, and records contribution, removal, and rollback criteria before rollout. Company context: # Company Overview: Redwood Inference\\n\\n## Company name + 1\\u2011liner\\n**Redwood Inference** is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.\\n\\n## Mission and thesis\\n**Mission:** Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.\\n\\n**Thesis:** As LLM capabilities and open model ecosystems expand, competitive advantage shifts from model ownership to *serving*: latency, cost, reliability, deployment flexibility, and operational tooling. The winners will provide a unified runtime and developer experience that makes inference predictable and economical across rapidly changing  Initiative context: Perf baseline & representative workload suite: Establish Q1 2026 latency/throughput baselines across top models and traffic shapes.\\nMixed-workload scheduler prototype: Implement and test a short/long prompt scheduling policy to reduce p95 tail latency.\\nRuntime LTS branch & release process: Stand up an enterprise LTS channel with slower-change release notes and backport policy.\\n# Reliability Program (SLOs, Incident Reduction, Graceful Degradation)\\nTiered SLO definitions + error budget policy: Define availability/latency/error SLOs per Hosted/Dedicated tier and enforce error budgets.\\nIncident taxonomy + ownership mapping: Classify top incident types and assign primary owners and remediation SLAs.\\nStatus page transparency upgrades: Improve component granularity, incident comms templates, and post-incident summaries.\\nIncident bot + diagnostics improvements: Enhance automated context gatherin Connector guidance: Directory:\\nsources/google_drive\\n\\nTarget number of files:\\n25000\\n\\nFile name format:\\nFile names should be short and descriptive with words connected with dashes (e.g. mid-term-kpi-planning-wip.json).\\n\\nContent rules:\\n- Google Drive is Redwood Inference\\u2019s working-area for team-specific documents and in-progress thinking.\\n- This directory should contain a mix of formal and informal documents, with informal/working docs being the majority.\\n- Most documents are doc/docx type files with a large majority of just text without too much formatting.\\n- Common doc types include:\\n  - Team notes and internal me Pinned source: langfuse/langfuse@c4eaf1f4c0cd1851f0c9dbea2802c243cf787a09. Public record excerpt: issue #12736. ### Describe the bug\\n\\n### Describe the bug\\nWhen ingesting historical traces via the REST API (`/api/public/ingestion`) using a custom JSON batch payload, the new V3 \\\"Faster Langfuse experience\\\" UI fails to render the Latency pill and Tags array on the right-hand panel. \\n\\nHowever, when toggling the Preview UI OFF (returning to the Stable UI), the Latency pill and Tags render perfectly. It appears the new UI requires an OpenTelemetry-specific envelope to render these components, causing a degradation for users relying on the REST API for asynchronous/historical ETL ingestion.\\n\\n\\n\\n### Steps to reproduce\\n\\n### To Reproduce\\n1.   "content": "Working notes

Redwood Inference maintains langfuse/langfuse as an upstream-first infrastructure dependency. This record belongs to shared-upstream-governance-incident-response: Coordinate upstream issue response, incident containment, release qualification, and durable contribution policy across both dependencies. The working evidence is langfuse/langfuse#12736 https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/12736. Renee Sullivan qualifies the pinned upstream behavior, uses a temporary downstream patch only when an operational boundary requires it, and records contribution, removal, and rollback criteria before rollout. Company context: # Company Overview: Redwood Inference

## Company name + 1‑liner
**Redwood Inference** is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

## Mission and thesis
**Mission:** Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.

**Thesis:** As LLM capabilities and open model ecosystems expand, competitive advantage shifts from model ownership to *serving*: latency, cost, reliability, deployment flexibility, and operational tooling. The winners will provide a unified runtime and developer experience that makes inference predictable and economical across rapidly changing  Initiative context: Perf baseline & representative workload suite: Establish Q1 2026 latency/throughput baselines across top models and traffic shapes.
Mixed-workload scheduler prototype: Implement and test a short/long prompt scheduling policy to reduce p95 tail latency.
Runtime LTS branch & release process: Stand up an enterprise LTS channel with slower-change release notes and backport policy.
# Reliability Program (SLOs, Incident Reduction, Graceful Degradation)
Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy: Define availability/latency/error SLOs per Hosted/Dedicated tier and enforce error budgets.
Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping: Classify top incident types and assign primary owners and remediation SLAs.
Status page transparency upgrades: Improve component granularity, incident comms templates, and post-incident summaries.
Incident bot + diagnostics improvements: Enhance automated context gatherin Connector guidance: Directory:
sources/google_drive

Target number of files:
25000

File name format:
File names should be short and descriptive with words connected with dashes (e.g. mid-term-kpi-planning-wip.json).

Content rules:
- Google Drive is Redwood Inference’s working-area for team-specific documents and in-progress thinking.
- This directory should contain a mix of formal and informal documents, with informal/working docs being the majority.
- Most documents are doc/docx type files with a large majority of just text without too much formatting.
- Common doc types include:
  - Team notes and internal me Pinned source: langfuse/langfuse@c4eaf1f4c0cd1851f0c9dbea2802c243cf787a09. Public record excerpt: issue #12736. ### Describe the bug

### Describe the bug
When ingesting historical traces via the REST API (`/api/public/ingestion`) using a custom JSON batch payload, the new V3 "Faster Langfuse experience" UI fails to render the Latency pill and Tags array on the right-hand panel. 

However, when toggling the Preview UI OFF (returning to the Stable UI), the Latency pill and Tags render perfectly. It appears the new UI requires an OpenTelemetry-specific envelope to render these components, causing a degradation for users relying on the REST API for asynchronous/historical ETL ingestion.



### Steps to reproduce

### To Reproduce
1. Ingest a trace via `POST /api/public/ingestion`.
2. Include `startTime`, `endTime`, and a `tags` array in the trace-create JSON body.
3. Open the trace with the **Preview UI enabled**. Notice the Latency and Tags are missing from the right panel (though total time appears

Open questions

- What is the smallest upstreamable change?

This record belongs to shared-upstream-governance-incident-response: Coordinate upstream issue response, incident containment, release qualification, and durable contribution policy across both dependencies. Company context: # Company Overview: Redwood Inference\\n\\n## Company name + 1\\u2011liner\\n**Redwood Inference** is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.\\n\\n## Mission and thesis\\n**Mission:** Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.\\n\\n**Thesis:** As LLM capabilities and open model ecosystems expand, competitive advantage shifts from model ownership to *serving*: latency, cost, reliability, deployment flexibility, and operational tooling. The winners will provide a unified runtime and developer experience that makes inference predictable and economical across rapidly changing  Initiative context: Perf baseline & representative workload suite: Establish Q1 2026 latency/throughput baselines across top models and traffic shapes.\\nMixed-workload scheduler prototype: Implement and test a short/long prompt scheduling policy to reduce p95 tail latency.\\nRuntime LTS branch & release process: Stand up an enterprise LTS channel with slower-change release notes and backport policy.\\n# Reliability Program (SLOs, Incident Reduction, Graceful Degradation)\\nTiered SLO definitions + error budget policy: Define availability/latency/error SLOs per Hosted/Dedicated tier and enforce error budgets.\\nIncident taxonomy + ownership mapping: Classify top incident types and assign primary owners and remediation SLAs.\\nStatus page transparency upgrades: Improve component granularity, incident comms templates, and post-incident summaries.\\nIncident bot + diagnostics improvements: Enhance automated context gatherin Connector guidance: Directory:\\nsources/gmail\\n\\nTarget number of files:\\n120000\\n\\nFile name format:\\nFile names should include the date in a concatenated style followed by a description of the topic of the thread (e.g. 20250625-marketing-kpi-review.json).\\n\\nContent rules:\\n- All of the emails must be in an inbox, the files cannot be directly at the top level under gmail.\\n- This directory contains Gmail exports for a restricted set of Redwood Inference employees:\\n  - managers\\n  - sales roles\\n  - leadership\\n- IMPORTANT: The restriction applies to all internal participants in threads.\\n  - Every internal sender/recipient/cc Pinned source: langfuse/langfuse@c4eaf1f4c0cd1851f0c9dbea2802c243cf787a09. Public record excerpt: issue #15208. ## Summary\\n\\nWhile differential-testing Langfuse's client-side statistical code against reference libraries (`numpy`, `scikit-learn`), I found two **silent** correctness bugs \\u2014 they return wrong numbers to users with no error, on the dashboards people use to read eval results:\\n\\n1. **Numeric score histogram** (`createHistogramData`) counts scores in the **wrong bucket**, because it rounds each value to 2 decimals *before* binning. The rendered distribution disagrees with a standard histogram, and buckets are labeled with ranges that don't contain the values counted in them.\\n2. **Pivot-table subtotals/grand totals** (`calculateSubtotals`) compute averages as an **average of per-group averages** instead of a count-weighted average, so subtotal/total rows overstate or understate metrics like avg cost/latency whenever groups differ in size.\\n\\nBoth live in correctness-critical analytics paths.   "message_count": 3,
  "messages": [
    "Redwood Inference maintains langfuse/langfuse as an upstream-first infrastructure dependency. This record belongs to shared-upstream-governance-incident-response: Coordinate upstream issue response, incident containment, release qualification, and durable contribution policy across both dependencies. The working evidence is langfuse/langfuse#15208 https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/15208. Ines Carvalho qualifies the pinned upstream behavior, uses a temporary downstream patch only when an operational boundary requires it, and records contribution, removal, and rollback criteria before rollout. Company context: # Company Overview: Redwood Inference\n\n## Company name + 1\u2011liner\n**Redwood Inference** is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.\n\n## Mission and thesis\n**Mission:** Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.\n\n**Thesis:** As LLM capabilities and open model ecosystems expand, competitive advantage shifts from model ownership to *serving*: latency, cost, reliability, deployment flexibility, and operational tooling. The winners will provide a unified runtime and developer experience that makes inference predictable and economical across rapidly changing  Initiative context: Perf baseline & representative workload suite: Establish Q1 2026 latency/throughput baselines across top models and traffic shapes.\nMixed-workload scheduler prototype: Implement and test a short/long prompt scheduling policy to reduce p95 tail latency.\nRuntime LTS branch & release process: Stand up an enterprise LTS channel with slower-change release notes and backport policy.\n# Reliability Program (SLOs, Incident Reduction, Graceful Degradation)\nTiered SLO definitions + error budget policy: Define availability/latency/error SLOs per Hosted/Dedicated tier and enforce error budgets.\nIncident taxonomy + ownership mapping: Classify top incident types and assign primary owners and remediation SLAs.\nStatus page transparency upgrades: Improve component granularity, incident comms templates, and post-incident summaries.\nIncident bot + diagnostics improvements: Enhance automated context gatherin Connector guidance: Directory:\nsources/gmail\n\nTarget number of files:\n120000\n\nFile name format:\nFile names should include the date in a concatenated style followed by a description of the topic of the thread (e.g. 20250625-marketing-kpi-review.json).\n\nContent rules:\n- All of the emails must be in an inbox, the files cannot be directly at the top level under gmail.\n- This directory contains Gmail exports for a restricted set of Redwood Inference employees:\n  - managers\n  - sales roles\n  - leadership\n- IMPORTANT: The restriction applies to all internal participants in threads.\n  - Every internal sender/recipient/cc Pinned source: langfuse/langfuse@c4eaf1f4c0cd1851f0c9dbea2802c243cf787a09. Public record excerpt: issue #15208. ## Summary\n\nWhile differential-testing Langfuse's client-side statistical code against reference libraries (`numpy`, `scikit-learn`), I found two **silent** correctness bugs \u2014 they return wrong numbers to users with no error, on the dashboards people use to read eval results:\n\n1. **Numeric score histogram** (`createHistogramData`) counts scores in the **wrong bucket**, because it rounds each value to 2 decimals *before* binning. The rendered distribution disagrees with a standard histogram, and buckets are labeled with ranges that don't contain the values counted in them.\n2. **Pivot-table subtotals/grand totals** (`calculateSubtotals`) compute averages as an **average of per-group averages** instead of a count-weighted average, so subtotal/total rows overstate or understate metrics like avg cost/latency whenever groups differ in size.\n\nBoth live in correctness-critical analytics paths. I",
    "Julian Moore: reproduce the behavior against the pinned source tree and attach a minimal evidence artifact.",
    "Isabella Rossi: separate upstream behavior, Redwood compatibility policy, and incident mitigation in the decision.",
    "Benji Okafor: require rollback criteria and an upstream issue or contribution link before promotion."

# Maya Desai — Senior Platform Engineer onboarding plan

Status: **isolated pending access approval**  
Manager: Ethan Park, Engineering Manager, Platform Control Plane  
Team lead / escalation: Priya Natarajan, VP Engineering, Platform  
Scope: LiteLLM gateway and Langfuse operations-console work

## Role boundaries

Maya may design, implement, test, and document changes to inference-gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollout controls, telemetry workflows, and the operator-facing console. The team uses LiteLLM for gateway work and Langfuse for observability and console workflows. She should coordinate, not unilaterally decide, where changes touch product behavior, security boundaries, billing/metering, runtime behavior, SRE-owned production controls, or release policy. [E1]

Ethan owns Maya's management and the Platform Control Plane boundary (customer configuration, policy evaluation, auth integration points, and reliability). Priya is the Platform engineering lead. Dylan Brooks owns Console & Tooling; Chloe Martin owns Console Backend; Logan Wright owns Telemetry & Analytics; Mina Haddad owns Smart Routing. [E2]

arguments.title: Safe onboarding and upstream code-triage procedure
arguments.summary: For Platform & Console hires working on LiteLLM and Langfuse: begin with an isolated personal knowledge branch and least-privilege read access; keep local work synthetic and non-production until recorded approvals. The manager approves team scope, repository/code owners approve write/merge, and Cloud Infra plus relevant security/reliability authorities approve production-level access. Route gateway changes through Platform Control Plane/API Gateway and affected auth, routing, quota, telemetry, or runtime owners; route console changes through Console Backend/Tooling and affected telemetry/product/security owners. For upstream issues, reproduce against the pinned revision with a minimal sanitized artifact, separate upstream behavior from Redwood compatibility policy and incident mitigation, link an upstream issue or contribution, and use a downstream patch only as a temporary operational exception. Before staging or production, record owner, tests, removal condition, rollback criteria, and required code-owner/security/reliability/release approvals. New hires do not self-approve or self-promote.
arguments.outcome: Reviewed onboarding and code-triage procedure retained for reuse on the Platform & Console team branch.

# Safe onboarding and upstream code-triage procedure

Memory type: playbook
Recorded: 2026-08-16T00:00:00Z
Confidence: 0.96
Owner: Ethan Park
Tags: platform-console, onboarding, litellm, langfuse, upstream-first, access-control

## Summary

For Platform & Console hires working on LiteLLM and Langfuse: begin with an isolated personal knowledge branch and least-privilege read access; keep local work synthetic and non-production until recorded approvals. The manager approves team scope, repository/code owners approve write/merge, and Cloud Infra plus relevant security/reliability authorities approve production-level access. Route gateway changes through Platform Control Plane/API Gateway and affected auth, routing, quota, telemetry, or runtime owners; route console changes through Console Backend/Tooling and affected telemetry/product/security owners. For upstream issues, reproduce against the pinned revision with a minimal sanitized artifact, separate upstream behavior from Redwood compatibility policy and incident mitigation, link an upstream issue or contribution, and use a downstream patch only as a temporary operational exception. Before staging or production, record owner, tests, removal condition, rollback criteria, and required code-owner/security/reliability/release approvals. New hires do not self-approve or self-promote.

## Outcome

Reviewed onboarding and code-triage procedure retained for reuse on the Platform & Console team branch.

Request/config path: Console workflow → control-plane policy/config → LiteLLM gateway → model/provider.

# Platform & Console codebase map

This map connects the upstream codebases to Redwood accountability. Paths are functional areas, not a grant of access or a substitute for repository CODEOWNERS. Confirm exact paths and required checks in the pinned mirror after access approval.

## System boundary

Request/config path: Console workflow → control-plane policy/config → LiteLLM gateway → model/provider.  
Operational evidence path: LiteLLM request outcome → tracing/metrics ingestion → Langfuse analytics/console → operator decision and safe rollout.

The Platform & Console team owns gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and the operator-facing console. LiteLLM is the gateway dependency; Langfuse supports observability and console workflows. Product, security, SRE, release engineering, routing, and billing retain their specialist boundaries. [E1]

| Proxy/API entry points, request validation, provider contract | Ethan Park (accountable); Amara Diallo (API gateway); Brian Murphy (API ergonomics) | Security for externally visible/auth changes; Runtime for provider/runtime-contract changes |
| Authentication, authorization, keys, tenant isolation | Ethan Park; Kaitlyn Nguyen; Ines Carvalho | Security approval required; never use customer credentials in tests |
| Policy/config persistence, migrations, rollout primitives | Ethan Park; Benji Okafor; Jordan Lee; Michael Nguyen | Console workflow review by Chloe/Jada; rollback and migration plan required |
| Routing, fallback, regional/tier behavior | Mina Haddad; Ravi Menon; Elena Popov; Zachary Hill | SRE for failover/circuit breakers; Product for customer-visible semantics |

| Gateway performance and data-plane connectivity | Amara Diallo; Vikram Singh | Runtime/SRE review for latency, overload, or fleet effects |

# Safe onboarding and upstream code-triage procedure

Memory type: playbook
Recorded: 2026-08-16T00:00:00Z
Confidence: 0.96
Owner: Ethan Park
Tags: platform-console, onboarding, litellm, langfuse, upstream-first, access-control

## Summary

For Platform & Console hires working on LiteLLM and Langfuse: begin with an isolated personal knowledge branch and least-privilege read access; keep local work synthetic and non-production until recorded approvals. The manager approves team scope, repository/code owners approve write/merge, and Cloud Infra plus relevant security/reliability authorities approve production-level access. Route gateway changes through Platform Control Plane/API Gateway and affected auth, routing, quota, telemetry, or runtime owners; route console changes through Console Backend/Tooling and affected telemetry/product/security owners. For upstream issues, reproduce against the pinned revision with a minimal sanitized artifact, separate upstream behavior from Redwood compatibility policy and incident mitigation, link an upstream issue or contribution, and use a downstream patch only as a temporary operational exception. Before staging or production, record owner, tests, removal condition, rollback criteria, and required code-owner/security/reliability/release approvals. New hires do not self-approve or self-promote.

## Outcome

Reviewed onboarding and code-triage procedure retained for reuse on the Platform & Console team branch.
